question:
Let $y(x)$ satisfy: $\frac{dy}{dx} + y \tan x = \sin x$.

(a) Find the general solution for $y(x)$.
(b) Evaluate the particular solution if $y\left( \frac{\pi}{4} \right) = 2$.
(c) Determine all values of $x$ (in $-\frac{\pi}{2} < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$) where $y(x)$ attains a local minimum.
explanation:
(a) Linear equation with $P(x) = \tan x$, $Q(x) = \sin x$
Integrating factor: $IF = e^{\int \tan x dx} = 1/\cos x$
Multiply through:
$\frac{d}{dx}(y/\cos x) = \tan x$
Integrate: $y/\cos x = -\ln|\cos x| + C$
$y(x) = - \cos x \ln|\cos x| + C \cos x$

(b) $y(\pi/4) = 2$ yields $C = 2\sqrt{2} - 1/2 \ln 2$
Particular solution: $y(x) = -\cos x \ln|\cos x| + (2\sqrt{2} - 1/2 \ln 2) \cos x$

(c) Critical points: $y'(x) = 0 \Rightarrow y = \cos x$
Substitute into solution: $|\cos x| = e^{D-1}$
$y''(x) \leq 0$, so local minima only at endpoints in given interval.

options.A:
(a) $y=\cos x\ln|\cos x|+C\cos x$
(b) $C=2\sqrt2+\frac12\ln2$
(c) Local minimum at $x=0$
options.B:
(a) $y=-\cos x\ln|\cos x|+C\sin x$
(b) $C=2\sqrt2-\frac12\ln2$
(c) Local minimum at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$
options.C:
(a) $y=-\cos x\ln|\cos x|+C\cos x$
(b) $C=2\sqrt2+\frac12\ln2$
(c) Local minimum at $x=0$
options.D:
(a) $y=-\cos x\ln|\cos x|+C\cos x$
(b) $C=2\sqrt2-\frac12\ln2$
(c) No local minimum inside $-\frac{\pi}{2}
